nodes.summary: A list $E$ of ordered pairs of vertices, read as directed edge occurrences, is balanced when every vertex $x$ occurs as the first component of exactly as many entries of $E$ as it occurs as the second component, counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Balanced edge list

nodes.summary: Given a directed adjacency graph $G$ and a function $R$ assigning to each vertex $u$ a list $R(u)$ of vertices, the edge list of $R$ is the list of pairs $(u, w)$, one for each entry $w$ of $R(u)$, taken over the vertices $u$ in the order of the vertex enumeration of $G$ and, for each $u$, in the order of $R(u)$. A repeated entry gives a repeated pair.
nodes.title: Edge list of an adjacency function

nodes.summary: The edge list of a directed adjacency graph $G$ is the list of pairs $(u, w)$, one for each entry $w$ of the adjacency list of $u$, taken over the vertices $u$ in the order of the vertex enumeration of $G$ and, for each $u$, in adjacency-list order. A repeated adjacency entry gives a repeated pair, so $G$ is read as a multigraph with one edge occurrence per entry.
nodes.title: Edge list of a directed graph

nodes.summary: For a vertex $x$, this assigns to an unordered pair $\{a, b\}$ the number $[x = a] + [x = b]$ of its endpoints equal to $x$, where $[P]$ is $1$ if $P$ holds and $0$ otherwise; in particular a loop $\{x, x\}$ gives $2$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity of a vertex in an unordered edge

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite list of edges of an undirected multigraph and let $W$ be an Euler path of $E$ from $s$ to $t$. Then every vertex other than $s$ and $t$ has even degree in $E$ (a loop counts twice); if $s \ne t$, then $s$ and $t$ have odd degree, and if $s = t$, every vertex has even degree.
nodes.title: Degrees of an undirected Euler path

nodes.summary: Let $W = (w_0, \dots, w_n)$ be a nonempty sequence of vertices with $w_0 = s$ and $w_n = t$, and consider the multigraph whose edges are the consecutive pairs $(w_{i-1}, w_i)$ for $1 \le i \le n$. In it every vertex other than $s$ and $t$ has even degree (a loop counts twice); if $s \ne t$, then $s$ and $t$ have odd degree, and if $s = t$, every vertex has even degree.
nodes.title: Degrees along a walk

nodes.summary: For a finite list $R$ of edges of an undirected multigraph and vertices $v$, $t$, the condition holds when for every vertex $x$ the number $\deg_R(x) + [x = v] + [x = t]$ is even, where $\deg_R$ is the degree in $R$ (a loop counts twice) and $[P]$ is $1$ if $P$ holds and $0$ otherwise. Thus if $v \ne t$, exactly $v$ and $t$ have odd degree, and if $v = t$, every degree is even.
nodes.title: Degree parity condition for two endpoints

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed adjacency graph, read as a multigraph with one edge per adjacency entry, and let $s$ be a vertex such that the source of every edge of $G$ is reachable from $s$. Then $G$ has an Euler circuit from $s$ if and only if $G$ is balanced, that is, every vertex is the source of exactly as many edge occurrences as it is the target of.
nodes.title: Euler circuit criterion for directed multigraphs

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed adjacency graph, read as a multigraph with one edge per adjacency entry, and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices such that the source of every edge of $G$ is reachable from $s$. Then $G$ has an Euler path from $s$ to $t$ if and only if $G$ is semi-balanced for $s$ and $t$: at $s$ one more edge occurrence leaves than enters, at $t$ one more enters than leaves, and every other vertex is the source of…
nodes.title: Euler path criterion for directed multigraphs

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite list of edges of an undirected multigraph (parallel edges and loops allowed), each given as a pair $(a, b)$, and let $s$, $t$ be vertices such that the first endpoint $a$ of every edge is reachable from $s$ along edges of $E$ traversed in either direction. Then $E$ has an Euler path from $s$ to $t$ if and only if, when $s \ne t$, exactly $s$ and $t$ have odd degree, and, when $s = t$, every…
nodes.title: Euler's theorem for undirected multigraphs

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed adjacency graph, read as a multigraph with one edge per adjacency entry, that is balanced (every vertex is the source of exactly as many edge occurrences as it is the target of), and let $s$ be a vertex such that the source of every edge of $G$ is reachable from $s$. Then the vertex sequence returned by Hierholzer's algorithm on $G$ from $s$ is an Euler circuit of $G$ from $s$.
nodes.title: Hierholzer's algorithm finds Euler circuits in directed multigraphs

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed adjacency graph, read as a multigraph with one edge per adjacency entry, and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices such that $G$ is semi-balanced for $s$ and $t$ (at $s$ one more edge occurrence leaves than enters, at $t$ one more enters than leaves, and at every other vertex as many leave as enter; at every vertex when $s = t$) and the source of every edge of $G$ is reachable from $s$. Then the vertex…
nodes.title: Hierholzer's algorithm finds Euler paths in directed multigraphs

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed adjacency graph, read as a multigraph with one edge per adjacency entry, and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices such that $G$ is semi-balanced for $s$ and $t$ and the source of every edge of $G$ is reachable from $s$. Then Hierholzer's algorithm on $G$ from $s$ costs exactly $|E|$ units, where $|E|$ is the number of edge occurrences of $G$, that is, the length of its edge list.
nodes.title: Running time of Hierholzer's algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed adjacency graph, read as a multigraph with one edge per adjacency entry, and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices such that $G$ is semi-balanced for $s$ and $t$. Then the vertex sequence $W$ returned by Hierholzer's algorithm on $G$ from $s$ starts at $s$ and ends at $t$, and the edge list of $G$ is a permutation of the list of consecutive pairs of $W$ followed by some further list of pairs. So $W$ is…
nodes.title: Hierholzer's algorithm returns a trail in a directed multigraph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed adjacency graph, read as a multigraph with one edge occurrence per adjacency entry, let $s$ be a vertex, and let $m$ be the number of edge occurrences of $G$, that is, the length of its edge list. Hierholzer's algorithm on $G$ from $s$ runs Hierholzer's recursion from $s$ with fuel $m + 1$, with the adjacency list of each vertex as its list of remaining out-neighbours and the empty list as…
nodes.title: Hierholzer's algorithm

nodes.summary: If a finite directed multigraph has an Euler circuit from some vertex $s$, then it is balanced: every vertex is the source of as many edge occurrences as it is the target of.
nodes.title: A directed multigraph with an Euler circuit is balanced

nodes.summary: A finite directed multigraph, read from its adjacency lists with each entry $w$ in the list of $u$ counted as one occurrence of the edge $u \to w$, is balanced when every vertex is the source of as many edge occurrences as it is the target of.
nodes.title: Balanced directed multigraph

nodes.summary: In a finite directed multigraph, a list of vertices $W$ is an Euler circuit from a vertex $s$ when it is an Euler path from $s$ to $s$: it starts and ends at $s$, and its list of consecutive pairs is a permutation of the list of edge occurrences of the graph.
nodes.title: Euler circuit in a directed multigraph

nodes.summary: In a finite directed multigraph, a list of vertices $W = (w_0, \dots, w_k)$ is an Euler path from $s$ to $t$ when $w_0 = s$, $w_k = t$, and its list of steps $(w_0, w_1), \dots, (w_{k-1}, w_k)$ is a permutation of the list of edge occurrences of the graph, so that each edge occurrence, counted with multiplicity, is traversed exactly once.
nodes.title: Euler path in a directed multigraph

nodes.summary: If a finite directed multigraph has an Euler path from $s$ to $t$, then it is semi-balanced for $s$ and $t$: counting edge occurrences, $s$ has one more outgoing than incoming edge, $t$ one more incoming than outgoing, and every other vertex is balanced (every vertex, when $s = t$).
nodes.title: A directed multigraph with an Euler path is semi-balanced

nodes.summary: A finite directed multigraph is semi-balanced for vertices $s$ and $t$ when, for every vertex $x$, the number of edge occurrences leaving $x$ plus $[x = t]$ equals the number entering $x$ plus $[x = s]$, where $[P]$ is $1$ if $P$ holds and $0$ otherwise. So for $s \ne t$, one more edge occurrence leaves $s$ than enters it, one more enters $t$ than leaves it, and every other vertex is balanced; for $s = t$ every…
nodes.title: Semi-balanced directed multigraph

nodes.summary: For a finite list $E$ of edges of an undirected multigraph and vertices $s$, $t$, a sequence of vertices $W = (w_0, \dots, w_n)$ is an Euler path of $E$ from $s$ to $t$ when $w_0 = s$, $w_n = t$, and the multiset of unordered pairs $\{w_{i-1}, w_i\}$ for $1 \le i \le n$ equals the multiset of the edges of $E$ taken as unordered pairs. Thus every edge is traversed exactly once, in either direction.
nodes.title: Euler path in an undirected multigraph

nodes.summary: For an edge $e = (a, b)$ and a vertex $v$, the other endpoint of $e$ at $v$ is $b$ if $a = v$, and $a$ otherwise; in particular a loop $(v, v)$ gives $v$.
nodes.title: Other endpoint of an edge

nodes.summary: For an element $e$ and lists $A$, $B$, $C$ of the same type, the list $e \cdot A \cdot B \cdot C$ is a permutation of $B \cdot e \cdot A \cdot C$, where $\cdot$ denotes concatenation and $e$ stands for the one-element list.
nodes.title: Moving a block of a list in front of an element is a permutation

nodes.summary: A list $E$ of ordered pairs of vertices is semi-balanced for vertices $v$ and $t$ when, for every vertex $x$, the number of pairs in $E$ with first component $x$ plus $[x = t]$ equals the number with second component $x$ plus $[x = v]$, where $[P]$ is $1$ if $P$ holds and $0$ otherwise. So for $v \ne t$, $v$ has one more outgoing than incoming occurrence, $t$ one more incoming than outgoing, and every other vertex…
nodes.title: Semi-balanced edge list

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be finite lists of edges of an undirected multigraph such that the multiset of edges of $A$, taken as unordered pairs, equals that of $B$. Then every vertex has the same degree in $A$ as in $B$.
nodes.title: Degrees depend only on the unordered edges

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a finite list of edges of an undirected multigraph, each an ordered pair of vertices, let $e = (a, b)$ be an edge in $R$, and let $x$ be a vertex. Then the degree of $x$ in $R$ equals the degree of $x$ in the list obtained from $R$ by removing the first occurrence of $e$, plus $[x = a] + [x = b]$, where $[P]$ is $1$ if $P$ holds and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Degree after removing an edge

nodes.summary: For a finite list $R$ of edges of an undirected multigraph, each given as a pair $(a, b)$, the degree of a vertex $x$ is the number of edges in $R$ whose first component is $x$ plus the number whose second component is $x$; parallel edges count separately and a loop $(x, x)$ counts twice.
nodes.title: Degree in an undirected edge list

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of undirected edges (ordered pairs of vertices) in which every vertex has even degree, and let $s$ be a vertex such that the first endpoint of every edge of $E$ is reachable from $s$ through edges of $E$. Then the vertex sequence returned by the undirected Hierholzer algorithm on $E$ from $s$ is an Euler path of $E$ from $s$ to $s$, that is, an Euler circuit at $s$.
nodes.title: Undirected Hierholzer's algorithm finds Euler circuits

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of undirected edges (ordered pairs of vertices) and $s$, $t$ vertices such that exactly $s$ and $t$ have odd degree in $E$ (no vertex has odd degree when $s = t$), and suppose the first endpoint of every edge of $E$ is reachable from $s$ through edges of $E$. Then the vertex sequence returned by the undirected Hierholzer algorithm on $E$ from $s$ is an Euler path of $E$ from $s$ to $t$.
nodes.title: Undirected Hierholzer's algorithm finds Euler paths

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of undirected edges and $s$, $t$ vertices such that exactly $s$ and $t$ have odd degree in $E$ (no vertex has odd degree when $s = t$), and suppose the first endpoint of every edge of $E$ is reachable from $s$ through edges of $E$. Then the undirected Hierholzer algorithm on $E$ from $s$ costs exactly $|E|$, the number of edges of $E$, in the cost model that charges one unit per removed edge.
nodes.title: Cost of the undirected Hierholzer algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of undirected edges and $s$, $t$ vertices such that exactly $s$ and $t$ have odd degree in $E$ (no vertex has odd degree when $s = t$). Then the vertex sequence $W$ returned by the undirected Hierholzer algorithm on $E$ from $s$ starts at $s$ and ends at $t$, and the consecutive pairs of $W$, as unordered pairs, form a sub-multiset of the edges of $E$ as unordered pairs: no edge is traversed more…
nodes.title: Undirected Hierholzer's algorithm returns a trail

nodes.summary: Given a list $E$ of undirected edges (ordered pairs of vertices) and a start vertex $s$, run the undirected Hierholzer recursion from $s$ on $E$ with an empty accumulator and fuel $|E| + 1$, and return the list of emitted vertices; its cost is the cost of that recursion.
nodes.title: Undirected Hierholzer's algorithm

nodes.summary: For a list $E$ of edges (ordered pairs of vertices), a vertex $x$ is reachable from a vertex $s$ when there are vertices $s = v_0, v_1, \dots, v_n = x$ with $n \ge 0$ such that for each $i < n$, $(v_i, v_{i+1})$ or $(v_{i+1}, v_i)$ belongs to $E$.
nodes.title: Reachability in an undirected multigraph

nodes.summary: If an ordered pair $e = (a, b)$ of vertices has $a = v$ or $b = v$, then the unordered pair $\{a, b\}$ equals $\{v, w\}$, where $w$ is the other endpoint of $e$ at $v$.
nodes.title: An edge at a vertex joins it to its other endpoint

nodes.summary: The ordered pair $(a, b)$ of vertices, viewed as the unordered pair $\{a, b\}$, so that $(a, b)$ and $(b, a)$ give the same unordered edge.
nodes.title: Unordered edge of an ordered pair

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a list of edges, $v$, $t$ vertices such that exactly $v$ and $t$ have odd degree in $R$ (no vertex when $v = t$), $A$ a list of vertices, and $f > |R|$ a fuel bound. Run the undirected Hierholzer recursion with fuel $f$ from $v$ on $R$ with accumulator $A$, and let $R'$ be the remaining edge list it returns and $c$ its cost. Then there is a vertex sequence $W$ starting at $v$ and ending at $t$ such that…
nodes.title: Invariant of the undirected Hierholzer recursion

nodes.summary: The recursion takes a fuel $f \in \mathbb{N}$, a vertex $v$, a list $R$ of remaining edges and an accumulator list $A$ of vertices, and returns a list of vertices and a list of remaining edges. With fuel $0$ it returns $A$ and $R$ unchanged. With fuel $f + 1$: if no edge of $R$ has $v$ as an endpoint, it returns $v$ prepended to $A$, together with $R$; otherwise, with $e$ the first such edge, it removes $e$ from…
nodes.title: Undirected Hierholzer recursion

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed multigraph, let $R$ assign to each vertex $u$ a list $R(u)$ of remaining out-neighbours, and let $E(R)$ be the list of remaining edge occurrences, one pair $(u, w)$ for each entry $w$ of $R(u)$. Let $v$ and $t$ be vertices, $\mathit{acc}$ a list of vertices and $n$ a natural number with $|E(R)| < n$, and suppose $E(R)$ is semi-balanced for $v$ and $t$: for every vertex $x$, the number…
nodes.title: Contract of Hierholzer's recursion

nodes.summary: Given a fuel $n$, a vertex $v$, an assignment $R$ of a list of remaining out-neighbours to each vertex, and a list $\mathit{acc}$ of vertices, the recursion returns a list of vertices and a new assignment, with a cost. With fuel $0$ it returns $(\mathit{acc}, R)$ at cost $0$. With fuel $n + 1$: if $R(v)$ is empty, it returns $v$ followed by $\mathit{acc}$ together with $R$, at cost $0$; otherwise $R(v)$ is $w$…
nodes.title: Hierholzer's recursion

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be nonempty vertex sequences, where $A$ ends at the vertex $a$ and $B$ starts at the vertex $b$. Then the steps of the concatenation $A B$ are the steps of $A$, followed by the step $(a, b)$, followed by the steps of $B$.
nodes.title: Steps of a concatenated walk

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence of vertices $W = (w_0, w_1, \dots, w_n)$, the steps of $W$ are the list of consecutive pairs $((w_0, w_1), (w_1, w_2), \dots, (w_{n-1}, w_n))$, in order. A sequence with at most one vertex has no steps.
nodes.title: Steps of a walk
Computer Science

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
